## The claim

Both alleles of the top-ranked biallelic candidate pair step 2 discovered are present at one-copy multiplicity, at posterior at least 0.95 each.

**Prediction if true.** The k-mer genotype of each of the two alleles puts posterior >= 0.95 on the heterozygous class, so each allele sits on one of the two copies rather than on both or on neither.

**What would refute it.** Either allele is not called single-copy at that posterior. This is a dosage statement and is not evidence of trans either way: read-backed phasing of this pair is impossible and no population statistic replaces it.
